newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks remain higher in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks remain higher in late trade.

text.p: Taiwan share prices remained higher in late Monday trade on a technical rebound led by plastics and constructions, brokers said.
With 45 minutes left, the index was up 99.09 points or 1.19 percent at 8,401.34. Turnover was a heavy T$71 billion.
Plastics led the rebound, rising 3.34 percent as the Economic Daily News reported on Monday that Formosa Plastics group may build a petrochemical complex in Australia.
Formosa officials declined to comment on the report.
Formosa Plastics surged T$3 to T$71.

Construction shares rose 2.78 percent as the Economic Daily News reported on Monday that the Finance Ministry was considering relaxing rules on banks' investment in the property market. Ministry officials declined to confirm the report.

The paper said the ministry plans to revise the Banking Law to allow banks to invest in properties they do not occupy and set a ceiling for such investment at 40 percent of each bank's net asset value.
Currently, the law only allows banks to purchase properties for their own use.
"Allowing banks to have more flexible operations is a trend inevitable, and the construction sector should benefit most from this reported move," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
